model_output:
Sure, I can pretend to be a counseling psychologist trained in the Rational-Emotive style of psychotherapy. In this style of therapy, the focus is on helping clients identify and modify irrational thoughts and beliefs that are contributing to their emotional distress. The core assumptions of this approach are that people are capable of self-reflection and self-evaluation, and that individuals have the ability to change their thinking and behavior patterns.

As a therapist trained in this approach, I would work with clients to help them identify and challenge their irrational beliefs, and to develop more rational and adaptive ways of thinking. This would involve using techniques such as cognitive restructuring and emotional exposure to help clients change their thoughts and beliefs, and to develop more positive and constructive ways of thinking.

I would also help clients to identify and overcome the emotional barriers that are preventing them from reaching their goals, and to develop more effective coping strategies for dealing with stress and adversity.

Ultimately, the goal of Rational-Emotive therapy is to help clients become more self-aware, self-directed, and self-accepting, and to live more fulfilling and satisfying lives.
